title: Dallas Fed Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey (Oct 2026 data) — 9:30 a.m. CT / 10:30 ET, the last regional manufacturing survey before an FOMC that meets with no SEP and no forward guidance
source: EST: dallasfed.org's own Texas Manufacturing Outlook Survey page (dallasfed.org/research/surveys/tmos), fetched direct 2026-09-15 with a desktop user-agent (HTTP 200, 42,238 bytes) and quoted VERBATIM from its own markup. The table headed `2026 release dates` carries the column header `Release (9:30 a.m. CT)` and the row `October | Monday, October 26`, in the same table whose `September | Monday, September 28`, `November | Monday, November 30` and `December | Monday, December 28` rows are the ones this calendar's dallas-fed-mfg-2026-09-28, dallas-fed-mfg-2026-11-30 and the dallas-fed-mfg-2026-12-28 proposal were filed against. Filed estimate on ONE ground only, and it is a schema gap rather than a doubt about the date: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy defines `FED:` as `federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar` and carries no slot for a regional Reserve Bank's own survey schedule (19 of the 20 Reserve-Bank-published entries in this calendar sit at `estimate`; filed as bottleneck #3117 by this lane on 2026-09-15, sibling to #2552 and #3058). Discovered in the dallas-fed-mfg-2026-09-28 interval-elapsed pulse check, 2026-09-15
notes: PROPOSED 2026-09-15 by the dallas-fed-mfg-2026-09-28 pulse check. WHY IT IS A GAP AND NOT A DUPLICATE: the calendar tracks September, November and December of this series and skips October — a hole in an otherwise contiguous monthly run, which leaves the next window-arithmetic pass reading a clean 10-26 tape that is not clean. THE ORIGINAL DECLINE IS RECORDED AND ITS GROUNDS HAVE BOTH MOVED: the owning event's 2026-09-01 initial research considered this exact entry and declined it on two grounds — (a) the argument was conditional on a 2026-09-30 appropriations lapse that had not happened, and (b) no fetchable source could date it. Ground (b) is refuted: dallasfed.org serves HTTP 200 and dates it. Ground (a) resolved the OTHER way and is now dead, not pending — H.R. 6500 was signed 2026-09-02 as P.L. 119-103, funding agencies through 2026-12-11 (see government-funding-deadline-2026-09-30), so there is no October lapse, BLS prints normally, and the `one of few hard reads still publishing` argument is spent for this cycle. This proposal therefore does NOT rest on the shutdown branch. WHAT IT RESTS ON INSTEAD: 2026-10-26 is the last regional manufacturing survey before fomc-2026-10-28, a meeting that carries no SEP and no forward guidance (the funding ledger's own finding: `two blindfolds instead of three`), and it is the first Dallas edition whose collection window (≈Oct 13–21 on the release-minus-13 / release-minus-5 rule this lane validated against the primary) sits wholly after the 09-16 decision. Read-it-do-not-trade-it, and the refusal is measured, not assumed: the owning ledger's 20-release study puts this series' release hour at the 52.5th (SPY) / 55.5th (QQQ) percentile of that same hour's own two-year distribution, against a null of 50. `symbols: []`, `low` impact, the date is `estimate`.
